_comment: Dev/e2e plugin discovery config. Declares the in-stack mcp-server-mock as a builtin (compose-installed) MCP-app plugin 'echoer'. Mounted into the backend container; STANDMEET_PLUGINS points here. Prod leaves STANDMEET_PLUGINS unset -> no discovered plugins.

plugins._comment: wsfs —— server-filesystem rooted at /workspace with sandbox.workspace=true: exercises the per-session workspace lifecycle (#148). Reuses fsmcp's installed code; the host lazily binds a per-conversation /workspace dir, swept by the backend TTL cron.

netfetch / cagedfetch —— the control pair. SAME immutable code (/srv/plugins/fetch), opposite egress policy, so a difference in outcome can only come from the grant and not from the block being broken. Both keep the default <id>_ prefix (netfetch_fetch / cagedfetch_fetch): two mounts of one server MUST be distinguishable, and the prefix already says which grant each carries.

escapee —— adversarial: server-filesystem rooted at / (NO app-level restriction), so ONLY bwrap confines it. The escape spec drives it to actively attempt known breakout vectors (host config, docker.sock, path traversal). Everything outside the sandbox mounts must be unreachable.

koishi —— the Koishi POC (item 28): our stdio-MCP wrapper (koishi-mcp.js) boots Koishi headlessly and exposes the third-party koishi-plugin-base64 (by windbullet, MIT). base64_encode/base64_decode results are computed by the real plugin — a correct result proves a plugin from another ecosystem runs unmodified as a StandMeet block. Pure compute, so allow_net:false. Credit: infra/plugins/koishi/CREDITS.
